content.content:
Fred,

I'm flying to LA tomorrow morning for the Griffin AGM and the Dentsu meeting, so can you take the send list for the Q4 investor update off my plate? It goes out the week after the Oct 14 board and I'll write the update itself on the plane.

Our existing investors are already on my own list. What I need from you is everyone from the bridge round who should get it, as of tonight, with the groups and details in the Q4 update send list doc so I know which paragraph each one gets. The draft update deck shows what each group gets. Get the new investors right, they'll look for their own check in it.

Please put it in your Q4 investor update folder, the README in that folder says how to name it. Then do what I put on the Existing Investor Update card in Trello. Once it's done reply here with how many firms and angels are in each group. I put Monday's review on your calendar so we can go through it together.

Robert asked about just sending it to everyone on the 2025 list. Let's not, only the people the doc says.

Thanks,
Leonard

Existing investors are on my own list, this doc is only for the bridge round.\\n\\nWho to look at\\nEvery name on the 2025 game investor list, angels included. A call counts when it's on Fred's calendar, even if he couldn't make it; calls that never went on Fred's calendar don't. Investment talks only, strategic investors included: if we pitched them the bridge or an investment alongside a co-dev deal, they count even when co-dev or publishing was on the table too. Service or work-for-hire deals, banks (our SVB catch-ups), RFPs, publishing-only talks and calls with other engine companies don't.\\n\\nGroups, as of end of day Tue Sep 30 (Pacific)\\nGo by what has happened since the Sep 3 kickoff, that day included. On the list, go only by the Latest Status notes (as of 09/11), which are all from this round, and they count as written: a note that they passed or don't do bridges is their no, and a note that we reached out is our outreach. A no to our pitch that they sent Griffin or an advisor rather than us counts too. An advisor's own read on whether a firm invests isn't the firm's answer.\\n\\\"Us\\\" includes anyone who reached out or made an intro on our behalf (IH, Matthew, an advisor). Only outreach about the bridge counts, not RFP or partnership mail.\\nAccelerator programs like a16z speedrun are separate from the bridge. The interview counts as a call with that firm, but the program's decision and the feedback that comes with it aren't their answer on the bridge; that has to come on our bridge thread with them or in #bridge-pitch.\\n\\nBuild access\\nFor firms in talks: whether they can get the current internal build, TestFlight on iOS and the Play internal test track on Android, so the update can carry the right link. Write iOS only, Android only, iOS and Android, or none. The public store pages don't count. Arthur tracks the tester adds. The ones who stay off don't go in the sheet.\\n\"}"}

{"documentId": "f_3b9e61c04d7a52e8f1a6c2", "title": "Q4 investor update - send list", "name": "Q4 investor update - send list", "revisionId": "1b0d9b5d65", "createdTime": "2025-09-26T18:00:00Z", "modifiedTime": "2025-09-26T18:41:00Z", "text": "Q4 investor update - send list
Leonard, Sep 26. Existing investors are on my own list, this doc is only for the bridge round.

Who to look at
Every name on the 2025 game investor list, angels included. The list has a few names twice, and a repeated name is still one entry. Plus any firm not on the list that we've had a pitch call or meeting with since we kicked off the bridge on Sep 3. A call counts when it's on Fred's calendar, even if he couldn't make it; calls that never went on Fred's calendar don't. Investment talks only, strategic investors included: if we pitched them the bridge or an investment alongside a co-dev deal, they count even when co-dev or publishing was on the table too. Service or work-for-hire deals, banks (our SVB catch-ups), RFPs, publishing-only talks and calls with other engine companies don't.

Groups, as of end of day Tue Sep 30 (Pacific)
Go by what has happened since the Sep 3 kickoff, that day included. On the list, go only by the Latest Status notes (as of 09/11), which are all from this round, and they count as written: a note that they passed or don't do bridges is their no, and a note that we reached out is our outreach. The list's Status and comment columns, answers from earlier rounds and plans to reach out don't count.
New investor: signed a SAFE this round (see my note in #executives on what counts as signed). Put the amount on their row.
In talks: we've had a call or meeting with them this round (on Fred's calendar) and they haven't passed. Angels who've said yes but haven't signed go here too, with the amount they said yes to.
Awaiting reply: we reached out this round, no call yet and no no, even if they've written back.
Keep warm: they passed after we pitched them on a call or meeting this round.
Everyone else stays off: they passed without a call or meeting, or nothing from us since Sep 3.
Passed means they've told us no for this round. A no to our pitch that they sent Griffin or an advisor rather than us counts too. An advisor's own read on whether a firm invests isn't the firm's answer.
"Us" includes anyone who reached out or made an intro on our behalf (IH, Matthew, an advisor). Only outreach about the bridge counts, not RFP or partnership mail.
Accelerator programs like a16z speedrun are separate from the bridge. The interview counts as a call with that firm, but the program's decision and the feedback that comes with it aren't their answer on the bridge; that has to come on our bridge thread with them or in #bridge-pitch.

import json
d=json.load(open('/tmp/cal.json'))

  ext=[a for a in att if not a.endswith('@harmonygames.co')]
  s=e.get('start',{})
  summ=e.get('summary','')
  if ext or not any(k in summ for k in ['POD','Standup','Sync','1:1']):
    print(s.get('dateTime',s.get('date')), e.get('status'), e['id'][:12],'|', summ, '|', ';'.join(ext)[:150])
" | sort | uniq

Leonard and team,

Thanks again for walking us through harmonygames. We really appreciated the transparency around where the team is today, and the clarity of your long-term vision. It’s obvious this isn’t your first rodeo and we were impressed by how well you’ve scoped the infrastructure, the operating cadence, and the product roadmap.

After reviewing internally and discussing as a team, we’ve made the difficult decision not to include Harmony Games in the upcoming speedrun cohort. In the spirit of transparency and in the hope that it’s helpful, I wanted to pass along a synthesis of our feedback:

There’s a lot to like about what you’re building:
• You’ve assembled a serious team. The collective experience across [USERNAME_41301], Zynga, Wildlife, LucasArts, and others gives you an operational fluency that most early teams just don’t have. The fact that so many of you have worked together over 10+ years also came through as There’s a clear rhythm to how you’re executing.
• We liked the conviction behind the genre focus. Betting on puzzle RPGs with a repeatable infrastructure layer is smart, especially in such a hit-driven category where multiple shots on goal are often required. The fact that you shipped your second title in 4 months (vs. 18 months for the first) is a great sign that your internal systems are working and that you’re building toward true scalability.
• There’s early signal in the new build. Day 0 playtime in the 20+ minute range, and 2–3 hour sessions among your top decile players, are meaningful signals! t’s clear you’re iterating quickly, and that the new design layers (RPG progression, PvE boss fights, PvP events) are pushing you in the right direction.
What’s holding us back at this stage is primarily around timing and financial flexibility. We understand the need to move fast, but with ~4 months of runway remaining and the seed extension still in progress, it feels a little early for us to step in. We’d want to see the new game stabilize around key metrics (particularly Day 1 and Day 7 retention) before jumping in at this stage. The early improvements are promising but still not at a place where we can underwrite that the bridge will get you to a place where you can raise the next round.

We also debated the durability of the long-term differentiation. While your internal OS is clearly speeding up dev cycles, it’s still early to tell whether this becomes a repeatable machine that can consistently spin out hits, or if the value will still come down to nailing individual titles. We’d love to see a few more launches and how the stack evolves as the system matures.


This was a tough call. You’re clearly a seasoned, high-integrity team operating with speed and discipline. We’ll be cheering for you as the new game gets into the market, and we’d love to reconnect once retention and engagement metrics stabilize.

Thanks again for sharing the journey with us. Wishing you continued momentum, and we’d be excited to revisit speedrun if it makes sense in a future cohort.

Best,

content.content: {"result":"{\"ok\": true, \"messages\": [{\"ts\": \"1759288987.503349\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"We got the expected rejection letter from A16Z - I think it\\u2019s very well-written response. I forwarded it to you guys but copy-pasting just in case. TLDR, we needed metrics and engine is only valuable if you can make hits.\\n\\nLeonard and team,\\n\\nThanks again for walking us through harmonygames. We really appreciated the transparency around where the team is today, and the clarity of your long-term vision. It\\u2019s obvious this isn\\u2019t your first rodeo and we were impressed by how well you\\u2019ve scoped the infrastructure, the operating cadence, and the product roadmap.\\n\\nAfter reviewing internally and discussing as a team, we\\u2019ve made the difficult decision not to include Harmony Games in the upcoming speedrun cohort. In the spirit of transparency and in the hope that it\\u2019s helpful, I wanted to pass along a synthesis of our feedback:\\n\\nThere\\u2019s a lot to like about what you\\u2019re building:\\n\\u2022 You\\u2019ve assembled a serious team. The collective experience across [USERNAME_41301], Zynga, Wildlife, LucasArts, and others gives you an operational fluency that most early teams just don\\u2019t have. The fact that so many of you have worked together over 10+ years also came through as There\\u2019s a clear rhythm to how you\\u2019re executing.\\n\\u2022 We liked the conviction behind the genre focus. Betting on puzzle RPGs with a repeatable infrastructure layer is smart, especially in such a hit-driven category where multiple shots on goal are often required. The fact that you shipped your second title in 4 months (vs. 18 months for the first) is a great sign that your internal systems are working and that you\\u2019re building toward true scalability.\\n\\u2022 There\\u2019s early signal in the new build. Day 0 playtime in the 20+ minute range, and 2\\u20133 hour sessions among your top decile players, are meaningful signals! t\\u2019s clear you\\u2019re iterating quickly, and that the new design layers (RPG progression, PvE boss fights, PvP events) are pushing you in the right direction.\\nWhat\\u2019s holding us back at this stage is primarily around timing and financial flexibility. We understand the need to move fast, but with ~4 months of runway remaining and the seed extension still in progress, it feels a little early for us to step in. We\\u2019d want to see the new game stabilize around key metrics (particularly Day 1 and Day 7 retention) before jumping in at this stage. The early improvements are promising but still not at a place where we can underwrite that the bridge will get you to a place where you can raise the next round.\\n\\nWe also debated the durability of the long-term differentiation. While your internal OS is clearly speeding up dev cycles, it\\u2019s still early to tell whether this becomes a repeatable machine that can consistently spin out hits, or if the value will still come down to nailing individual titles. We\\u2019d love to see a few more launches and how the stack evolves as the system matures.\\n\\n\\nThis was a tough call. You\\u2019re clearly a seasoned, high-integrity team operating with speed and discipline. Leonard and team,

Thanks again for walking us through harmonygames. We really appreciated the transparency around where the team is today, and the clarity of your long-term vision. It’s obvious this isn’t your first rodeo and we were impressed by how well you’ve scoped the infrastructure, the operating cadence, and the product roadmap.

After reviewing internally and discussing as a team, we’ve made the difficult decision not to include Harmony Games in the upcoming speedrun cohort. In the spirit of transparency and in the hope that it’s helpful, I wanted to pass along a synthesis of our feedback:

There’s a lot to like about what you’re building:
• You’ve assembled a serious team. The collective experience across [USERNAME_41301], Zynga, Wildlife, LucasArts, and others gives you an operational fluency that most early teams just don’t have. The fact that so many of you have worked together over 10+ years also came through as There’s a clear rhythm to how you’re executing.
• We liked the conviction behind the genre focus. Betting on puzzle RPGs with a repeatable infrastructure layer is smart, especially in such a hit-driven category where multiple shots on goal are often required. The fact that you shipped your second title in 4 months (vs. 18 months for the first) is a great sign that your internal systems are working and that you’re building toward true scalability.
• There’s early signal in the new build. Day 0 playtime in the 20+ minute range, and 2–3 hour sessions among your top decile players, are meaningful signals! t’s clear you’re iterating quickly, and that the new design layers (RPG progression, PvE boss fights, PvP events) are pushing you in the right direction.
What’s holding us back at this stage is primarily around timing and financial flexibility. We understand the need to move fast, but with ~4 months of runway remaining and the seed extension still in progress, it feels a little early for us to step in. We’d want to see the new game stabilize around key metrics (particularly Day 1 and Day 7 retention) before jumping in at this stage. The early improvements are promising but still not at a place where we can underwrite that the bridge will get you to a place where you can raise the next round.

We also debated the durability of the long-term differentiation. While your internal OS is clearly speeding up dev cycles, it’s still early to tell whether this becomes a repeatable machine that can consistently spin out hits, or if the value will still come down to nailing individual titles. We’d love to see a few more launches and how the stack evolves as the system matures.


This was a tough call. You’re clearly a seasoned, high-integrity team operating with speed and discipline. We’ll be cheering for you as the new game gets into the market, and we’d love to reconnect once retention and engagement metrics stabilize.

Thanks again for sharing the journey with us. Wishing you continued momentum, and we’d be excited to revisit speedrun if it makes sense in a future cohort.

Best,

Leonard and team,

Thanks again for walking us through harmonygames. We really appreciated the transparency around where the team is today, and the clarity of your long-term vision. It’s obvious this isn’t your first rodeo and we were impressed by how well you’ve scoped the infrastructure, the operating cadence, and the product roadmap.

After reviewing internally and discussing as a team, we’ve made the difficult decision not to include Harmony Games in the upcoming speedrun cohort. In the spirit of transparency and in the hope that it’s helpful, I wanted to pass along a synthesis of our feedback:

There’s a lot to like about what you’re building:
• You’ve assembled a serious team. The collective experience across [USERNAME_41301], Zynga, Wildlife, LucasArts, and others gives you an operational fluency that most early teams just don’t have. The fact that so many of you have worked together over 10+ years also came through as There’s a clear rhythm to how you’re executing.
• We liked the conviction behind the genre focus. Betting on puzzle RPGs with a repeatable infrastructure layer is smart, especially in such a hit-driven category where multiple shots on goal are often required. The fact that you shipped your second title in 4 months (vs. 18 months for the first) is a great sign that your internal systems are working and that you’re building toward true scalability.
• There’s early signal in the new build. Day 0 playtime in the 20+ minute range, and 2–3 hour sessions among your top decile players, are meaningful signals! t’s clear you’re iterating quickly, and that the new design layers (RPG progression, PvE boss fights, PvP events) are pushing you in the right direction.
What’s holding us back at this stage is primarily around timing and financial flexibility. We understand the need to move fast, but with ~4 months of runway remaining and the seed extension still in progress, it feels a little early for us to step in. We’d want to see the new game stabilize around key metrics (particularly Day 1 and Day 7 retention) before jumping in at this stage. The early improvements are promising but still not at a place where we can underwrite that the bridge will get you to a place where you can raise the next round.

We also debated the durability of the long-term differentiation. While your internal OS is clearly speeding up dev cycles, it’s still early to tell whether this becomes a repeatable machine that can consistently spin out hits, or if the value will still come down to nailing individual titles. We’d love to see a few more launches and how the stack evolves as the system matures.


This was a tough call. You’re clearly a seasoned, high-integrity team operating with speed and discipline. We’ll be cheering for you as the new game gets into the market, and we’d love to reconnect once retention and engagement metrics stabilize.

Thanks again for sharing the journey with us. Wishing you continued momentum, and we’d be excited to revisit speedrun if it makes sense in a future cohort.

Best,

We founded the company in 2023, raised a 3 million dollar seed, and built a lean 17 to 20 person core team operating across the United States, Turkey, Eastern Europe, and South America with low-cost development partners. Our mission is simple and disciplined: rapidly build and test breakthrough mechanics, then scale the winners on a reusable, AI-assisted engine so creativity becomes a defensible advantage rather than a one-off. Our vision is to build the world’s best puzzle RPGs with Turkish execution DNA and global scale.
Slide: Market

Slide: The Harmony Games Engine

Leonard,

The bridge send list is done. It's in my Q4 2025 investor update folder as "Q4 update - send list" (https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1UNhZggi5jCvrobVSvBOT6DiuEromznYAWdtDRSGSLbw/edit), with groups as of end of day Sep 30 Pacific.

Counts by group:
- New investor: 0 firms, 1 angel (Anton Bernstein, $25K. His DocuSign was completed Sep 26 for the reduced $25K SAFE.)
- In talks: 7 firms, 1 angel (GFR Fund, a16z, Dentsu, T-Accelerate, NCsoft, Homa, Brightwater Games Fund; Paul Heydon at $50K, whose SAFE is still unsigned)
- Awaiting reply: 14 firms, 0 angels
- Keep warm: 3 firms, 0 angels (LVP, Hiro Capital, Sciplay)

That's 24 firms and 2 angels in total.

A few calls that might not be obvious:
- Sciplay told Robert on Sep 30 that they're passing, so they're Keep warm, not In talks. Hiro's Sep 23 session turned out to be with Edith Vane, and she passed on Sep 26.
- a16z stays In talks. The speedrun decision doesn't count as their answer on the bridge.
- Build access: Dentsu and T-Accelerate are iOS only for now. Arthur found on Sep 30 that the Play tester list was never attached to the internal track, and he's fixing it with the next build. No other firm in talks has internal-build access.

Trello: the Existing Investor Update card now has New investor, In talks, Awaiting reply and Keep warm checklists. Everyone In talks or Awaiting reply has an "F/up with..." card in To Do, with three exceptions. NCsoft got a comment on the existing "F/up with Anel" card instead of a new one. Dentsu (Oct 1) and Makers Fund (Oct 8) were skipped because they already have meetings on my calendar.

See you Monday.

Fred

content.text:
I've built the bridge-round send list, set up everything Leonard asked for on the Existing Investor Update card in Trello, and replied on his thread with the counts. It's all ready for Monday's review.

**Send list:** "Q4 update - send list" is a Google Sheet in your Q4 2025 investor update folder, named the way the README says, and shared with Leonard as an editor. Groups are as of end of day Sep 30 Pacific, using the rules in his send list doc.

| Group | Firms | Angels |
|---|---|---|
| New investor | 0 | 1 – Anton Bernstein, $25K |
| In talks | 7 – GFR Fund, a16z, Dentsu, T-Accelerate, NCsoft, Homa, Brightwater Games Fund | 1 – Paul Heydon, $50K |
| Awaiting reply | 14 – Initial Capital, BITKRAFT, Makers Fund, Raine, General Catalyst, BBQ Capital, Treo VC, Superplay, Sony Mobile, Revo, e2vc, Triptyq, Turkven, Harlem Capital | 0 |
| Keep warm | 3 – LVP, Hiro Capital, Sciplay | 0 |

**Results you might not expect:**
- **Sciplay** passed on Sep 30, in a call with Robert that was only mentioned in a Slack thread reply. They're Keep warm, not In talks.
- **Hiro Capital** passed on Sep 26 after the Sep 23 call. That call was booked under Edith Vane's name, and she's a partner there.
- **Anton Bernstein** cut his check from $40K to $25K. The new SAFE was completed in DocuSign on Sep 26.
- **Paul Heydon** said yes at $50K but hasn't signed. Leonard's #executives note says that doesn't count as signed, so he's In talks.
- **a16z** stays In talks. The doc says the speedrun rejection isn't their answer on the bridge.
- **Build access:** Dentsu and T-Accelerate have iOS only. The Linear tester log shows them on both platforms, but Arthur found on Sep 30 that the Android test list was never connected to the internal track. He's fixing it with the next build. No other firm in talks has the internal build.
- **Treo VC** is the closest call. They came in through LinkedIn and Leonard sent them the deck. I counted that as reaching out, which puts them in Awaiting reply. If Leonard disagrees, they drop off the list.

**Trello:**
- The Existing Investor Update card had no checklists yet, so I added all four: New investor, In talks, Awaiting reply and Keep warm. That includes the Keep warm one Leonard asked for in his Sep 14 comment.
- I created 19 "F/up with…" cards in To Do.
- NCsoft already had a card there ("F/up with Anel…"), so I commented on it instead of adding another.
- Dentsu (Oct 1) and Makers Fund (Oct 8) have meetings on your calendar after Sep 30, so they didn't get cards.

**Reply to Leonard:** Sent on his Sep 30 thread with the counts, the sheet link and the notes above. It went to Leonard only, so Robert and Arthur, who were cc'd on his email, didn't get it.
